name: Hilkiah (Father of Eliakim, steward under King Hezekiah)
title: Father of the Steward Eliakim
summary: Hilkiah is known as the father of Eliakim, who served as steward (palace administrator) under King Hezekiah of Judah. He is mentioned in connection with the Assyrian crisis when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem. Although little is known about Hilkiah personally, his son Eliakim played a crucial role in negotiations with the envoys of the Assyrian king.

keyEvents.title: Eliakim is mentioned as the son of Hilkiah
keyEvents.description: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, is described as the administrator over the king's house under King Hezekiah, indicating that Hilkiah belonged to a prominent family in Judah.

keyEvents.title: The Assyrian Crisis at Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, was sent together with Shebna and Joah to meet Rabshakeh, the envoy of the Assyrian king Sennacherib, at the walls of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Messengers to the Prophet Isaiah
keyEvents.description: After Rabshakeh's threatening speech, King Hezekiah sent Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, and others to the prophet Isaiah to seek advice and intercession.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's parallel account about Eliakim
keyEvents.description: In the book of Isaiah, the same events are recounted where Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, plays a central role in negotiations with the Assyrians and in contact with the prophet Isaiah.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's prophecy concerning Eliakim
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah delivered a prophecy that Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, would be appointed to Shebna's position as steward and become like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Eliakim sent to Isaiah according to the book of Isaiah
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah sent Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, along with the chief priests to the prophet Isaiah to seek the Lord's word during the Assyrian siege.
